:::{#exm-matrix-induced-norm}
#### A matrix-induced norm calculation

Take the [positive definite matrix](#def-positive-definite)
$\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
of @exm-matrix-induced-inner-product
and the vector $\vx = (1, 2)$.
Then

$$
\ba
\norm{\vx}_{\matr{A}}
&= \sqrt{\iprod{\vx}{\vx}_{\matr{A}}}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-induced-norm)}
\\
&= \sqrt{\tp{\vx} \matr{A} \vx}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-induced-inner-product)}
\\
&= \sqrt{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}}
&& \text{(substitute the vector and the matrix)}
\\
&= \sqrt{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 2 \\ 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 2 \end{bmatrix}}
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \sqrt{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= \sqrt{1 \cd 4 + 2 \cd 5}
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \sqrt{14}.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

The [Euclidean norm](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-euclidean-norm) of the same vector is
$\norm{\vx} = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{5}$,
so the $\matr{A}$-norm of this vector is larger than its Euclidean norm.

<!-- no-figure: the example computes one norm of one vector -->

:::
